text:
erin: Heads-up — been noodling on continuous-batcher tradeoffs for heterogeneous GPUs. Thinking of a lightweight pipeline-splitter that routes requests into a hotpath slab vs a warm lane to reduce head-of-line latency for short/kv-hot requests. sketch later, want quick reality-check.

aj: sketch pls — short summary of the decision surface?

erin: short: early classifier uses (seq_len bucket, kv-cache-hit, model-variant compatibility, client SLAs) -> route to HOT slab (tight latency, small batch target, preemptible) or WARM slab (max throughput, large-batches). key tradeoffs: increased routing complexity, potential KV cache scattering, and admission handshake changes.

sam: KV cache locality is my main worry — splitting can scatter cache entries across GPUs and raise miss rate. any ideas to preserve locality?

erin: agreed. two mitigations: 1) affinity_tag (hash by tenant+recent-prefix) to keep a client on same slab when possible; 2) per-slab lightweight bloom filter for recent KV residency so we prefer slab with hits. plus a short stickiness window (e.g., 60s) to avoid churn.

kevin: complexity tradeoff aside, what's the operational cost when we misroute? i.e., warm->hot vs hot->warm misroutes cost?

erin: misroute cost summary: warm->hot (move small batch to hot) usually increases throughput cost but keeps latency low — acceptable. hot->warm (sending latency-sensitive request into big-batch lane) risks p99 tail due to batch wait. fallback strategy: if wait exceeds threshold (configurable, e.g., 5ms) then preempt batch or direct to hot with partial-batch fastpath. also reclaim credits if preemptions frequent.

tanya: what telemetry should we add to know this is working?

aj: minimal metric set: p50/p99 latency per-slab, effective_batch_size, kv_cache_hit_ratio per-slab, per-tenant cold_miss_rate, aborted_prefetch_count, gpu_occupancy, avg_wait_ms in queue. add a counter for route_decision and misroute_penalty.

luis: can we simulate this before touching runtime? small sim to measure cache hit delta vs latency gains.

ops-bot: queued simulation job: id=2026-03-batcher-sim-42, namespace=canary, status=queued.

sam: also fairness: hot path could be abused by noisy tenants. need a hot_credits per-tenant with depletion and decay.

erin: yes — design idea: hot_credits refilled at rate R, decremented on each route_to_hot. when credits exhausted, route falls back to warm and client is marked for score-decay. stickiness bounded so a tenant can't hog hot forever.

kevin: admission API changes? keep it minimal. we don't want big proto churn.

aj: agreed. a simple RouteDecision payload should be enough. paste proto?

erin: paste:
```proto
message RouteDecision {
  string request_id = 1;
  enum Target { HOT = 0; WARM = 1; }
  Target target = 2;
  int32 deadline_hint_ms = 3; // optional hint to admission
  string affinity_tag = 4;
}
```

tanya: nice. can we also tag traces with route info so we can correlate misroutes to p99 spikes? @ops-bot

ops-bot: added `route_decision` trace tag and per-request route_reason enum to canary traces for namespace `batcher-canary` — will stream to observability.

luis: next steps & timeline?

erin: I'll wire a micro-sim this week that models mixed traffic (short/long/kv-heavy). Plan: 1 week of sims + tuning, then 2-week staging canary with synthetic and sampled production traffic. If sims look good, follow up RFC for admission-api + rollout playbook.

aj: :thumbsup:

kevin: please add experiments to record `misroute_penalty` and `cold_miss_tail` as first-class metrics.

tanya: add rollback criterion to playbook: rollback if p99 increases >20% sustained over 10m for any critical route.

sam: sounds good. thanks all.
